method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (the text's no where it says no; NOTHING-kind where it does not answer); the dates in one module, chapter 5 in a second, liability, defences and damages in a third, cases in two more; five regulative rules (DEONTIC functions: the notice of claim and its late-notice continuation, the respondent's s 54 response, the s 61 offer and the claimant's answer, the s 114D nomination period) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Civil Law (Wrongs) Act 2002 (ACT), A2002-40, Republication No 77 (R77), effective 16 May 2026, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/A2002-40.txt; division 8A.1A.2 (ss 114BBB-114BBD) commenced 16 May 2026 (inserted by A2026-7 s 10). The Civil Law (Wrongs) Regulation 2003 is not deposited: the Act's own fallback periods and figures are used.

seat: the claimant: the person bringing a claim for damages for personal injury in the ACT (the injured person; after a death, a member of the dead person's family or the estate; for mental harm, the relative who suffered it; for child abuse, the person abused as a child; for a child, the parent or guardian giving notice) (clwa-precourt.l4, clwa-liability.l4)
focus: the provisions a claimant meets: the personal injuries pre-court procedure (ch 5), and the liability, defences, damages and costs rules that decide whether, whom and for how much a claimant can sue

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run clwa-dates.l4 ; l4 run clwa-precourt.l4 ; l4 run clwa-liability.l4 ; l4 run clwa-precourt-cases.l4 ; l4 run clwa-liability-cases.l4
checks.result: 257 assertions written, 257 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07, after the verification fixes); deliberately wrong assertions in scratch copies showed as failed
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.
